The Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament (HMMT) is a U.S. high-school competition for advanced olympiad-style contestants.

The Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament (HMMT) February 2026 problem set was extracted from the official website [68]. The PDFs were processed with DeepSeek-OCR-2 [94], after which all problems were manually verified and corrected. HMMT is entirely student-organized, by students at Harvard, MIT, and nearby schools, many of whom are HMMT alumni themselves.
Founded in 1998, HMMT is one of the largest and most prestigious high school competitions in the world.
The February tournament includes three individual tests:
Algebra test, which covers topics from high school algebra and number theory.
Geometry test, which covers high school Euclidean geometry.
Combinatorics test, which covers high school combinatorics.
Each individual test is 10 problems and 50 minutes long, where all answers are single values (i.e. short answers).
The Team Round is a 60-minute, 10-problem test where all members of a team work together.
The Guts Round is an 80-minute team event with 36 short-answer questions on an assortment of subjects, of varying difficulty and point values.
The February problems are challenging, ranging from mid-AIME problems to problems which would be suitable for national olympiads such as USAMO.
The February Team round is quite difficult; some of the problems are comparable to the hardest problems on national olympiads such as USAMO.
